html:
The Tanzimat, meaning "reorganisation", was a period of reforms in the Ottoman Empire from 1839 to 1876. It aimed to save the empire from defeat and break-up by making the state more modern and central.

It began with the Edict of Gülhane in 1839, which promised all subjects security of life and property, fair taxes and regular conscription, whatever their religion. A second decree in 1856 went further in promising equality to Christians and Jews. The ground had been prepared by Sultan Mahmud II, who destroyed the Janissaries in 1826.

  • New law codes and secular courts, partly on French models.
  • State schools and a modern civil service.
  • Reforms of land ownership, taxes and the army.
  • Railways, telegraphs and the Imperial Ottoman Bank.

Results were mixed. Many Muslims resented the equality decrees, and the empire sank into debt. The era closed with the constitution of 1876, soon suspended by Abdul Hamid II.
sum: The Tanzimat, meaning "reorganisation", was a period of reforms in the Ottoman Empire from 1839 to 1876. It aimed to save the empire from defeat and break-up by making the state more modern and central.
